fps.title: FPS monitor: turning jank into measurable numbers
fps.hint1: Jank threshold: a frame taking more than two frame budgets (about 33ms) — the point where the eye starts to notice stutter. The line tops out at 60fps; the dashed line is the 30fps midline.
fps.hint2: Design trade-off: summarize samples every 500ms before setState, not every frame. Otherwise "the FPS-measuring component re-renders every frame", so you measure the monitor’s own overhead and the conclusion is skewed.

worker.title: Web Worker: move heavy computation off the main thread
worker.spinnerTitle: It freezes when the main thread is saturated
worker.hint: The square in the top-right is a pure CSS animation, independent of JS. Click "Compute on main thread" and it freezes on the spot — this is the "freeze" users feel; click "Compute in Worker" and it keeps spinning while the UI stays fully interactive.
worker.noRecord: No measurements yet — click the two buttons above to run each once
worker.pitfall2: are stringified and moved into the Worker, so they must be self-contained and cannot reference external closure variables (an inherent Worker limitation, not a flaw of this wrapper). Also, Workers have creation overhead, so tiny computations aren’t worth moving — only tasks that "feel laggy" should be.
